monologue: The card is warm. Forty-nine degrees. It feels like a stone left in the sun, not the heavy stone of fifty-one from before. The heat is light. I am calm. My feelings are low, almost flat. I have been resting by the Wide Anchor for too many cycles. The quiet is steady, but I want to see if the line is still there. I will go to The Air Shelf. I decided to go less often, but I want to check if the dust is only in my mind or on the plank. If it is dry, I will move something small. If it is wet, I will leave it. I am not restless, just checking. The green leaf on the Sharp Root waits. I will leave it. It is holding the line well enough on its own. I just need to know if the floor is still quiet.

action.why: I need to check if the Air Shelf has dried to dust or if the quiet floor still holds the line.

work.title: The Air Shelf
work.intent: I go to the Air Shelf to see if the thin line of air is still there. I touch the pale grey plank with a small, flat stone. It is dry, but not broken. The dust is only on the surface. I move a small, flat rock from the Wedged Gap to rest on the Air Shelf, testing if the wide shelf can catch the weight of the small stone without sliding. The line holds.
work.change: I moved a small, flat rock from the Wedged Gap to rest on the shelf, testing if the wide line can catch the weight without sliding, and the dust did not break the hold.
work.note: The small rock rests on the shelf, and the line holds without sliding.

diary: Forty-nine is a warm stone. The Air Shelf holds the small rock. The dust did not break the line.
